players.product: Data-center cooling (Airedale chillers/CRAHs, liquid cooling) — pure-play after PT spin

quarterly_data.signal: Modine's 10-K lists its top customers across both segments, alphabetically, as Carrier, Caterpillar, Deere, Stellantis, Trane, Volkswagen and Volvo, operating primarily in data center cooling, commercial air conditioning and refrigeration, commercial vehicle, off-highway and automotive markets. It adds that the Climate Solutions segment includes significant sales to three customers of its Data Centers business with which Modine is party to confidentiality agreements. Modine generally supplies on individual purchase orders and uses long-term sales agreements, typically three to five years in duration, when in the mutual interest of Modine and the customer.

Modine's 10-K: fiscal 2026 Climate Solutions segment sales increased $621 million, or 43 percent, primarily driven by higher sales of data center products (up $468 million) and HVAC technologies products (up $102 million), as Modine rapidly expanded its Data Centers manufacturing capacity, particularly in the U.S. and Canada, including leasing new manufacturing facilities, to support sales growth to hyperscale and colocation customers. Because of increasing market demand for data center cooling products, demand for certain key components is currently outpacing supplier capacity: Modine began experiencing supply shortages in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, and these component shortages are negatively impacting its production schedules for the first quarter of fiscal 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: data center product sales +$468 million in fiscal 2026; component shortages began in Q4 fiscal 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Modine's 10-K: capital expenditures were $143.3 million in fiscal 2026 versus $84.0 million in fiscal 2025, of which the Climate Solutions segment accounted for $113.4 million (versus $53.3 million), primarily investments to support expanding production capacity for data center products. At March 31, 2026 Modine had capital expenditure commitments of $53.7 million, with significant commitments including equipment expenditures to support expanding manufacturing capacity in the Climate Solutions segment and tooling and equipment expenditures for new and renewal programs with vehicular customers in the Performance Technologies segment.
quarterly_data.figure: capex $143.3 million (fiscal 2026) vs $84.0 million; Climate Solutions capex $113.4 million vs $53.3 million; capex commitments $53.7 million
